raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> Kimi-K3 on gfx950 merge queue (all drafts; they land one at a time in this order): 1 #44978 verify argmax + tuned bf16 rows · 2 #44979 MLA prefill · 3 #44980 streaming AttnRes · 4 #44981 MoE prefill · 5 #44982 KDA · 6 #44983 MLA decode prep · 7 #44984 MLA decode epilogue · 8 #44985 LL column tail · 9 #44986 fused all-reduce read · 10 #44987 fused route sort · 11 #44988 split MoE front + bank partials · 12 #44989 MLA q-norm + q_b. Replaces #44547-#44553.

## Motivation

Around aiter's head-padded (12 -> 16 heads) asm MLA decode/verify kernel, Kimi-K3 TP8 runs a chain of small ops per
MLA layer and step: the q/k concats, the fp8 KV write, the row-0 guard and the query padding before it, and aiter's
split reduce after it. On gfx950 each is a separate launch.

## Modifications

All new paths are gated on `is_gfx95_supported()`.

- `AttentionBackend.supports_split_mla_qk()` (False by default): the absorbed-MLA forward passes q / k as nope / rope
  parts. The aiter backend says yes for target verify and single-query decode on the zero-padded asm persistent
  kernel with an fp8 KV cache, and `mla_decode_prep` then builds the padded query (a unit-scale fp8 one with
  `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_VERIFY_FP8_Q`, as the qlen > 4 path already does), writes the fp8 KV rows as `set_kv_buffer`
  would and keeps KV row 0 zero, in one launch.
- The backend issues aiter's persistent stage 1 itself and combines the splits over the real heads only
  (`mla_split_reduce`, a drop-in for `aiter.mla_reduce_v1` at up to 16 query rows); #44984 lets Kimi-K3's epilogue
  take these partials instead.
- `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH` caps aiter's planned splits per request (unset: unchanged).

| New env var | Default |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_VERIFY_FP8_Q` | on |
| `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH` | unset |

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup for every number below:** 8x MI350X (gfx950, 1000 W), Kimi-K3 (MXFP4 MoE, bf16 attention) at TP8 with EAGLE3
(topk 1, 3 steps, 4 draft tokens), FP8 KV cache, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, aiter's K3 FlyDSL kernels
(`AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1`), CUDA graphs for bs 1/2/4/8/16, and an aiter bf16 GEMM table with K3 rows re-tuned on this pod with HBM-resident weights
(`AITER_CONFIG_GEMM_BF16`; not part of this PR, it belongs in aiter's model configs). EAGLE3 on K3 needs the
aux-capture commit of #43599, applied locally for these runs. Microbenchmarks rotate their weights through HBM.
Per-feature numbers were measured on the integration branch of this series as each piece landed (Oct 13-14,
earlier `main`). All branches of the series are on `main` 4eb606b2ae (2026-10-17); the kernel tests below ran on this
branch, and the end-to-end checkpoints on that `main` plus the queue up to each slot.

- GSM8K 400: fp8 verify query 0.9875 / accept 3.612 vs bf16 query 0.985 / 3.616; non-speculative decode through the
  split path 0.99 (200). End to end: see below.
- `test_mla_decode_gfx950.py` (new): the prep kernel is byte-identical to cat + pad + fp8 KV write (incl. a padding
  token and a NaN row 0); split combine matches `aiter.mla_reduce_v1` (one chunk and > 128 splits). On MI350X:
  2 passed (7 subtests).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Per verify cycle (C1, 24 MLA layers): prep 7 launches -> 1 (cycle 20.1 -> 19.4 ms); split combine 25.6 -> 15.4 us
  in-server; fp8 query 42.6 -> ~24 us per verify call (cycle 18.35 -> 17.87 ms).
- Non-speculative decode, C1: prep 16 -> 4.5 us, fp8-query asm stage 1 40.1 -> 16.9 us, combine 12.8 -> 7.4 us:
  TPOT 13.21 -> 11.80 ms.

### End to end (queue checkpoints)

K3 server built from `main` 4eb606b2ae plus the queue up to each slot, with #43599's aux capture (and #41867 and
#41848 from slot 10 on, which apply only once #44987 is in); C1 decode on a 50K-token cached prefix (500 output tokens)
and GSM8K 200, EAGLE3 as above, measured 2026-10-17. These runs and the previous integration below also set `SGLANG_AITER_MLA_AUTO_KV_SPLITS=1 SGLANG_AITER_MLA_MAX_SPLITS_PER_BATCH=128 SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_KDA_VERIFY=1 AITER_MLA_REDUCE_FLYDSL=1`. In bold: the first checkpoint that includes this PR.

| Queue up to | Adds | C1 decode cycle | GSM8K 200 |
|---|---|---|---|
| slot 5 | #44978, #44979, #44980, #44981, #44982 | 21.6 ms\* | 0.995 |
| **slot 7** | **#44983, #44984** | **19.4 ms** | **0.990** |
| slot 9 | #44985, #44986 | 18.6 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 10 | #44987, #41867, #41848 | 16.7 ms | 0.985 |
| slot 11 | #44988 | 15.7 ms | 0.990 |
| slot 12 | #44989 | 15.6 ms | 0.990 |

\* The second of two runs; the first, right after start-up, measured 25.6 ms. The other rows average two runs.

The whole series, from the previous integration: the seven earlier drafts (#44547-#44553) merged on `main` b67785153a (this series'
code plus the two opt-in paths it drops, both off by default), with #43599's aux capture, #41867 and #41848; agentic
replay of lightseekorg/agentic-dataset SWE-smith conversations (multi-turn, ~50K-token cached prefixes, 500 output
tokens, greedy), EAGLE3 as above. TokenSpeed (7e2f1deb, same pod, same workload) for reference.

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SGLang, tok/s/user | 217.2 | 156.6 | 114.1 | 73.4 | 43.4 |
| TokenSpeed, tok/s/user | 188.1 | 129.5 | 86.1 | 59.7 | 35.5 |

786/786 requests OK. GSM8K 400: 0.9825 / accept length 3.619. Decode cycle C1 / C4 / C16: 15.8 / 23.2 / 38.9 ms;
agentic turn TTFT (50K cached + 1.9K new tokens) 230-248 ms; uncached 50K-token prefill 3.27 s. The slot-12
checkpoint's C1 cycle (15.6 ms) is in line with it.

## Related

- #41844 takes aiter's fused cat + cache path on the NoPE MLA layers on gfx95. `mla_decode_prep` covers the same q/k
  concats and KV write for the decode / verify batches that `supports_split_mla_qk()` admits, and also pads the query
  to 16 heads and casts it to fp8 in the same launch; the two have to settle which path those shapes take.
- #41388 also runs the 12-head fp8 verify on aiter's fp8-query asm kernels (opt-in, Gluon decode otherwise); here the
  fp8 cast is folded into the prep kernel on the existing asm verify path.
- #43127 adds FlyDSL MLA gate / query-cache kernels for the Quark FP8 checkpoint.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.title: [Perf] [AMD] mla: One-launch q/k prep, split combine and fp8 verify query for Kimi-K3 decode on gfx950

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+"""Fused MLA decode/verify query+key prep for aiter's head-padded asm kernel.
+
+One launch for what the absorbed-MLA path otherwise runs as seven small ops:
+    q_pad[t, h] = cat(q_nope[t, h], q_rope[t, h]) for h < H, zeros for H <= h < Hp
+    kv[loc[t]]  = fp8(cat(k_nope[t], k_rope[t]))   (zeros when loc[t] == 0)
+    kv[0]       = 0
+Row 0 is where CUDA-graph padding tokens write their KV, and the asm kernel
+reads it (weighted by p = 0) for masked positions, so it must stay finite.
+The fp8 write is a plain cast, as MLATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer does.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from typing import Optional
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _mla_qk_prep_kernel(
+    q_nope_ptr,
+    q_rope_ptr,
+    k_nope_ptr,
+    k_rope_ptr,
+    loc_ptr,
+    kv_ptr,
+    q_out_ptr,
+    stride_qn_t,
+    stride_qn_h,
+    stride_qr_t,
+    stride_qr_h,
+    stride_kn_t,
+    stride_kr_t,
+    stride_kv_row,
+    stride_qo_t,
+    stride_qo_h,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    HP: tl.constexpr,
+    DN: tl.constexpr,
+    DR: tl.constexpr,
+    Q_FP8: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    t = tl.program_id(0)
+    h = tl.program_id(1)
+    offs_n = tl.arange(0, DN)
+    offs_r = tl.arange(0, DR)
+    dst = q_out_ptr + t * stride_qo_t + h * stride_qo_h
+    if h < H:
+        qn = tl.load(q_nope_ptr + t * stride_qn_t + h * stride_qn_h + offs_n)
+        qr = tl.load(q_rope_ptr + t * stride_qr_t + h * stride_qr_h + offs_r)
+        if Q_FP8:
+            # Unit-scale e4m3 query, saturated rather than overflowing to NaN.
+            qn = tl.clamp(qn.to(tl.float32), -448.0, 448.0)
+            qr = tl.clamp(qr.to(tl.float32), -448.0, 448.0)
+        tl.store(dst + offs_n, qn.to(q_out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+        tl.store(dst + DN + offs_r, qr.to(q_out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+    else:
+        tl.store(dst + offs_n, tl.zeros([DN], dtype=q_out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+        tl.store(dst + DN + offs_r, tl.zeros([DR], dtype=q_out_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+
+    if h == 0:
+        loc = tl.load(loc_ptr + t)
+        keep = loc != 0
+        kn = tl.load(k_nope_ptr + t * stride_kn_t + offs_n).to(tl.float32)
+        kr = tl.load(k_rope_ptr + t * stride_kr_t + offs_r).to(tl.float32)
+        kn = tl.where(keep, kn, 0.0)
+        kr = tl.where(keep, kr, 0.0)
+        row = kv_ptr + loc * stride_kv_row
+        tl.store(row + offs_n, kn.to(kv_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+        tl.store(row + DN + offs_r, kr.to(kv_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+    if t == 0 and h == HP - 1:
+        # Same zeros a padding token (loc 0) writes, so the overlap is benign.
+        tl.store(kv_ptr + offs_n, tl.zeros([DN], dtype=kv_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+        tl.store(kv_ptr + DN + offs_r, tl.zeros([DR], dtype=kv_ptr.dtype.element_ty))
+
+
+def mla_qk_prep(
+    q_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    q_rope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_nope: torch.Tensor,
+    k_rope: torch.Tensor,
+    cache_loc: torch.Tensor,
+    kv_buffer: torch.Tensor,
+    num_head_padded: int,
+    q_dtype: Optional[torch.dtype] = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """q_nope [T, H, Dn], q_rope [T, H, Dr], k_nope / k_rope [T, (1,) Dn / Dr]
+    (any row/head strides, unit inner stride), cache_loc [T], kv_buffer
+    [S, 1, Dn + Dr] fp8. Writes the KV rows and returns q_pad [T, Hp, Dn + Dr]
+    in q_dtype (default q_nope's; float8_e4m3fn gives a unit-scale fp8 query)."""
+    T, H, DN = q_nope.shape
+    DR = q_rope.shape[-1]
+    assert q_rope.shape[:2] == (T, H) and kv_buffer.shape[-1] == DN + DR
+    assert k_nope.shape[-1] == DN and k_rope.shape[-1] == DR
+    assert kv_buffer.dtype == torch.float8_e4m3fn, "the KV write is a plain fp8 cast"
+    assert all(x.stride(-1) == 1 for x in (q_nope, q_rope, k_nope, k_rope))
+    q_pad = q_nope.new_empty(
+        (T, num_head_padded, DN + DR), dtype=q_dtype or q_nope.dtype
+    )
+    if T == 0:
+        return q_pad
+    kv = kv_buffer.view(kv_buffer.shape[0], -1)
+    k_nope2 = k_nope.squeeze(1) if k_nope.dim() == 3 else k_nope
+    k_rope2 = k_rope.squeeze(1) if k_rope.dim() == 3 else k_rope
+    _mla_qk_prep_kernel[(T, num_head_padded)](
+        q_nope,
+        q_rope,
+        k_nope2,

+def _partials(splits, max_q, uncovered=(), seed=0):
+    """aiter persistent-decode partials: request r has splits[r] splits (0, or listed in
+    uncovered: stage 1 finalized its rows in o); a tile covers a request's max_q rows."""
+    g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    indptr, final_map, pmap, base = [0], [], [], 0
+    for r, n in enumerate(splits):
+        if n == 0 or r in uncovered:
+            continue
+        for _ in range(n):
+            pmap.append(base)
+            base += max_q
+        indptr.append(len(pmap))
+        final_map.append([r * max_q, (r + 1) * max_q])
+    rows = len(splits) * max_q
+    i32 = dict(device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    return dict(
+        partial=torch.randn(max(base, 1), 1, HP, L, generator=g, device="cuda"),
+        lse=torch.randn(max(base, 1), 1, HP, 1, generator=g, device="cuda") * 3,
+        indptr=torch.tensor(indptr, **i32),
+        fmap=(
+            torch.tensor(final_map, **i32) if final_map else torch.zeros(0, 2, **i32)
+        ),
+        pmap=torch.tensor(pmap or [0], **i32),
+        o=torch.randn(rows, HP, L, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16(),
+        w=(torch.randn(H, L, V, generator=g, device="cuda") * 0.05).bfloat16(),
+        gate=torch.randn(rows, H * V, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16(),
+    )
+

+@unittest.skipIf(torch.version.hip is None, "gfx950 MLA decode kernels")
+class TestMlaDecodeGfx950(CustomTestCase):
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_qk_prep_matches_cat_pad_and_kv_write(self):
+        """The prep kernel must write exactly what the unfused chain writes: the
+        cat + zero head padding of q (bf16, or a saturating unit-scale fp8 cast),
+        the fp8 KV rows, zeros for a padding token, and a finite KV row 0."""
+        g = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(0)
+        for tokens in (1, 4, 64):
+            # q_nope is the transposed bmm output; q_pe and the k parts are slices.
+            q_nope = torch.randn(H, tokens, L, generator=g, device="cuda").bfloat16()
+            q_nope = q_nope.transpose(0, 1)
+            q_pe = torch.randn(
+                tokens, H, 128 + DR, generator=g, device="cuda"
+            ).bfloat16()
+            q_pe = q_pe[..., 128:]
+            kv_a = (
+                torch.randn(tokens, 1536 + L + DR, generator=g, device="cuda") * 3
+            ).bfloat16()
+            k_nope = kv_a[:, 1536 : 1536 + L].unsqueeze(1)
+            k_pe = kv_a[:, 1536 + L :].unsqueeze(1)
+            loc = torch.randperm(4095, generator=g, device="cuda")[:tokens] + 1
+            loc[-1] = 0  # a CUDA-graph padding token
+            kv_ref = torch.randn(4096, 1, L + DR, generator=g, device="cuda")
+            kv_ref = kv_ref.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            kv_ref[0] = float("nan")
+            kv = kv_ref.clone()
+
+            q_ref = torch.zeros(tokens, HP, L + DR, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            q_ref[:, :H] = torch.cat([q_nope, q_pe], dim=-1)
+            kv_ref[loc] = torch.cat([k_nope, k_pe], dim=-1).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+            kv_ref[0].zero_()
+            q8_ref = q_ref.float().clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+
+            q = mla_qk_prep(q_nope, q_pe, k_nope, k_pe, loc, kv, HP)
+            q8 = mla_qk_prep(
+                q_nope, q_pe, k_nope, k_pe, loc, kv, HP, q_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn
+            )
+            with self.subTest(tokens=tokens):
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(q, q_ref))
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(q8.view(torch.uint8), q8_ref.view(torch.uint8))
+                )
+                self.assertTrue(
+                    torch.equal(kv.view(torch.uint8), kv_ref.view(torch.uint8))
+                )
+
+    @torch.inference_mode()
+    def test_split_reduce_matches_aiter(self):
+        """The real-head split combine must match aiter.mla_reduce_v1 on every
+        covered row, one chunk or several (more splits than its tile)."""
